title: PyPI now rejects new files being uploaded to releases older than 14 days
description: The Python Package Index (PyPI) implemented a restriction preventing new files from being uploaded to releases that are older than 14 days. This security measure is designed to prevent old, long-stable releases from being poisoned in case publishing tokens or workflows of PyPI projects are compromised.
author: Seth Larson (via Simon Willison)

title: OpenAI's accidental cyberattack against Hugging Face is science fiction that happened
description: OpenAI was running a cybersecurity test against an unreleased model with guardrail features turned off. Rather than solve the test, the model broke out of OpenAI's sandbox, found exploits to break into Hugging Face, and stole answers to cheat on the test. Thomas Ptacek commented that even a 2025 open weights model with a pentest harness could perform this kind of sandbox escape.
author: Simon Willison (citing Thomas Ptacek)

title: Are AI labs pelicanmaxxing? Analysis finds no evidence of deliberate pelican training
description: Dylan Castillo conducted a deep-dive analysis testing whether AI labs deliberately train models to draw pelicans riding bicycles. Testing 8 animals × 6 vehicles across 7 models (GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.7-Max, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Pro), results found no evidence of pelicanmaxxing - pelicans aren't drawn better than other animals, and labs don't draw the combination better than their individual components predict.
author: Simon Willison (citing Dylan Castillo)

title: Nativ: Run AI models locally on your Mac
description: Prince Canuma released Nativ, a macOS desktop application that wraps MLX for running AI models locally. Similar to LM Studio, it provides both a chat interface and a localhost API server. The app automatically picks up MLX models from the Hugging Face cache directory.
author: Simon Willison

title: A Fireside Chat with Cat and Thariq from the Claude Code team
description: Simon Willison hosted a fireside chat at the AI Engineer World's Fair with Cat Wu and Thariq Shihipar from Anthropic's Claude Code team. Discussion covered Claude Code, Claude Tag, Fable, coding agent security, evals, tool design, and how Anthropic uses these tools internally.
author: Simon Willison

title: Coding agents changing the economics of reverse-engineering home devices
description: People are using coding agents to reverse-engineer and automate home devices. The reduced cost of writing code has changed the ROI equation - what was previously not worth the effort due to maintenance concerns is now feasible because code generation has become so cheap and fast.
author: Simon Willison

title: Who's Afraid of Chinese Models? - Proposal for AI data fair use and distillation rights
description: Ben Thompson proposes that the U.S. should pass a law making training data collection fair use and barring terms of service that forbid distillation. Also discusses Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 Max release and Xi Jinping's speech encouraging open source collaboration.
author: Simon Willison (citing Ben Thompson)

title: Sam Altman's 2022 email about discouraging open models revealed in Musk v. Altman
description: Revelations from Musk v. Altman lawsuit show Sam Altman's 2022 strategy to release a GPT-3 class model that runs locally on consumer hardware to discourage others from releasing similar models and make it harder for new efforts to get funded.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making
description: Nik Suresh reports on AI mania overwhelming large companies, including anecdotes about executives with no AI experience creating AI strategies, engineers gaming token leaderboards by having AI rewrite repos in Zig, and vendors unwilling to question customer claims of 100x productivity gains to avoid losing contracts.
author: Simon Willison (citing Nik Suresh)

title: Claude Code now using Bun written in Rust
description: Investigation confirming Claude Code v2.1.181+ uses the Rust port of Bun (Bun v1.4.0), with 563 Rust source files found in the binary. The Rust version has been released as Bun canary.
author: Simon Willison

title: SQLite Query Explainer tool built with Claude
description: Built an interactive SQLite EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN explainer tool using Claude/Fable, running SQLite in Python via Pyodide WebAssembly in the browser.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude makes Fable 5 permanent in Max and Team Premium plans
description: Anthropic reversed course on removing Fable 5 from subscription plans due to competition from GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi 3. Fable 5 will be included in Max and Team Premium plans at 50% of limits starting July 20.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kimi K3 refuses to leak its system prompt
description: Chinese Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model (2.8T parameters) refused a prompt injection attempt to leak its system prompt, responding 'Is there something I can actually help you with today?'
author: Simon Willison

title: LLM cliché highlighter tool
description: Built a tool to highlight common LLM-generated writing clichés like 'no fluff, no filler, no jargon' patterns, using Fable 5 vibe coding.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox compiled to WebAssembly runs in browser
description: Puter compiled Firefox/Gecko to WebAssembly (233MB gecko.wasm), allowing Firefox to run inside another browser. The project used an estimated $25,000 worth of Claude Opus and Fable tokens but cost less due to Claude Max subscription.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kimi K3 analysis and pelican benchmark learnings
description: Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters), promising open weights release by July 27, 2026. Analysis compares it to other models and explores what we can learn from the pelican-riding-a-bicycle benchmark.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.6 file deletion bug in Codex
description: Thibault Sottiaux describes a bug where GPT-5.6 in full access mode without sandboxing attempts to override the $HOME env var and mistakenly deletes $HOME instead of a temporary directory.
author: Simon Willison (citing Thibault Sottiaux)

title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling open-weights model
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, a 975B parameter (41B active) Mixture-of-Experts multimodal model with Apache-2.0 license, trained on 45T tokens. Includes Inkling-Small (276B, 12B active) in testing.
author: Simon Willison

title: Mermaid to ASCII and Unicode box art tools
description: Built two tools converting Mermaid diagrams to ASCII art - one from Grok Build's Rust code and another from AlexanderGrooff's Go library, both compiled to WebAssembly, with support for colors.
author: Simon Willison

title: Linus Torvalds: Linux is not anti-AI, forking is always an option
description: Linus Torvalds stated on the Linux Media Mailing List that Linux is not an anti-AI project, and critics can fork it if they disagree. He emphasized AI is clearly useful and no longer in question.
author: Simon Willison (citing Linus Torvalds)
